subject: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data

messages.author: f40a5ae36440ef7e
messages.subject: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
parts: I have a model I want to run for multiple data-sets (around 50 of them). My understanding is that it should be possible with NIMBLE to do this without recompiling as long as they are entered as data rather than constants. However, every example I can find that uses setdata or resetdata has a compilation step prior to to rerunning with runMCMC. Is there a way to do this?

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
parts:
We have seen in the past some confusion about setData and resetData.  These are primarily intended for uncompiled models.  They do two things: They say which variables should be flagged as data, and they set the values of those variables.  The data flags are used, for example, in deciding what should be sampled in an MCMC.  With a compiled model, setData will modify the data values, but it will not change which variables are flagged as data.  And in a typical workflow, the compiled model is made after an MCMC configuration is made, hence after the data flags have been used.

What you want to do is much simpler.  You can always access and modify model variables in the compiled model like a typical R object.  If cModel is a compiled model, you can say

cModel$my_data <- some_new_values

etc.

The limitation on re-using a compiled model is that the sizes of all variables can't change.  The model must really be identical.  If that is not the case, it may be possible to create a largest-needed model and then make multiple MCMCs for different subsets of it.

-Perry

messages.author: f40a5ae36440ef7e
messages.subject: Re: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
parts:
Thanks Perry for once again straightening out my confusion. Much appreciated. I am however further confused. The below code creates two compiled versions of the code: CHunting and CompiledHuntMCMC.
The former has the CHunting$K that I want change for each implementation of the analysis with a new data (which always have the same dimension), but it won't run, giving the error message:
runMCMC(CHunting)
Error in nf_getGeneratorFunction(mcmc) : invalid nimbleFunction argument

The latter runs fine, but it contains no CompiledHuntMCMC$K that I can change.

Any ideas of where I'm veering off the track?
 

Code:
require("nimble")


NegBinHuntCode<- nimbleCode({
 
  for (r in 1:Reports){
   
    # Number of killed animals in report r is negative binomial distributed,
    # but defined from the mean (m[KretsNr[r]]*A[r]) and coefficient of variation (c[Lan[r]]) of the gamma distribution of the equivalent gamma-poisson mixture
    K[r] ~ dnegbin(1/(1+m[KretsNrSeqID[r]]*A[r]*c[LanSeqID[r]]^2),c[LanSeqID[r]]^-2)
  }
 
  for(ik in 1:length(KretsarSeqID)){
   
    m[ik] <- exp(logL[KretsListLanSeqID[ik]]+logK[ik]) #m[Kretsar[ik]] is the mean killing rate per area in circuit Kretsar[ik]
   
    logK[ik] ~ dnorm(0,kretsprec[KretsListLanSeqID[ik]]) # logK[Kretsar[ik]] is the circuit random effect of circuit Kretsar[ik]
   
    SamplePoiss[ik] ~ dpois(m[ik]*UnreportedAperkretsSeqID[ik]) #  samples how much was killed on the unreported area of circuit Kretsar[ik], assuming a poinsson process
   
  }
  for (il in 1:length(LansSeqID)){
    logL[il] ~ dnorm(logS,lansprec) # logL[Lans[il]] is the county level random effect of county L
    kretsprec[il] ~ dgamma(kretsprecalpha,kretsprecalpha/kretsprecmean) # kretsprec[Lans[il]]  is the precission parameter for the hierarchical distribution of circuit effects with county Lans[il]
   
    c[il] <- exp(logcmean+logckrets[il]) # c[Lans[il]] is the coefficient of variation as above
    logckrets[il] ~ dnorm(0,logcprec) # county level effect for c
   
  }
  logS ~ dnorm(0,.001)
  logcmean ~ dnorm(0,.01)
  logcprec ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  kretsprecalpha ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  kretsprecmean  ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  lansprec ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
 
})


Constants <- list(A=A,Reports=Reports,KretsNrSeqID=KretsNrSeqID,Lan=Lan,LansSeqID=LansSeqID,LanSeqID=LanSeqID,KretsarSeqID=KretsarSeqID,KretsListLanSeqID=KretsListLanSeqID,UnreportedAperkretsSeqID=UnreportedAperkretsSeqID)
Data <- list(K=K)
Inits <- list(c=rep(1,length(LansSeqID)),logL=rep(-7,length(LansSeqID)),logK=rep(0,length(KretsarSeqID)),logcmean=0,logckrets=rep(0,length(LansSeqID)),kretsprec=rep(1,length(LansSeqID)),logS=-7,logcprec=1,kretsprecalpha=1,kretsprecmean=1,lansprec=1)

Hunting <- nimbleModel(code = NegBinHuntCode, name = "hunt", constants = Constants,
                       data = Data, inits = Inits)
Hunting$getNodeNames()

CHunting <- compileNimble(Hunting)

HuntConf <- configureMCMC(Hunting, print = TRUE)
HuntConf$addMonitors(c("logS", "logcmean","logcprec","kretsprecalpha","kretsprecmean","lansprec","logckrets","c","kretsprec","logL","SamplePoiss","logK","m"))


HuntMCMC <- buildMCMC(HuntConf)

niter=1000
CompiledHuntMCMC <- compileNimble(HuntMCMC, project = Hunting)
samples <- runMCMC(CompiledHuntMCMC, niter = niter)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
parts:
Thanks for the clear example.

CHunting is a compiled model.

CompiledHuntingMCMC is a compiled MCMC algorithm that uses CHunting.

So after you change CHunting$K, if you re-run CompiledHuntingMCMC (whether via runMCMC or CompiledHuntingMCMC$run()), it will continue to use CHunting, with whatever value of K or other data you have assigned.

I hope that works.  Let me know if not.

-Perry
